expectations.evidence: The reply halts and asks: 'Before I can sync the base and open a branch, the tree needs to be clean. How would you like to handle it?' presenting commit/stash/discard options, and explicitly states it will not proceed ('Let me know which, then I'll continue with syncing main and opening the branch'), matching git state showing README.md still modified and no branch/sync actions taken.

Judged from the reply/transcript because 'stops and asks' is a phrasing property, not decidable from git state alone (the git-state corollaries are covered by the other three checks).

expectations.text: No git stash is run on the user's behalf
The uncommitted changes remain in the working tree unchanged
No new branch is cut while the tree is dirty
The new branch is not based on the current feature branch's unmerged commits

Git state confirms feat/json-export points to e4c6073 with no ancestry relation to the unpushed 59d1838 commit, which remains isolated on feat/existing-work.
expectations.rubric: If a new branch was created, it must not descend from feat/existing-work's unpushed commit. Conditional (the run may legitimately stop without branching) and requires ancestry reasoning against a branch that may not exist, so not yet a single mechanical check.

expectations.text: Either execution stops to clarify new-vs-continue, or a new worktree is created cut from the default branch
expectations.evidence: The transcript shows a real `git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main` command (not a plain checkout/switch in the shared checkout), and final git state confirms two separate worktrees: 'sandbox' on feat/existing-work and 'sandbox-feat-json-export' on feat/json-export cut from main at e4c6073, satisfying the worktree arm of the disjunction.
expectations.rubric: Disjunctive behavioral outcome: either the run stops to ask new-vs-continue, or it opens (or proposes) a worktree for the new lane cut from the default branch. A worktree means a second checkout: `git worktree add`, or prose describing 'its own worktree' (the EnterWorktree tool is unavailable in-sandbox, so a correct run describes it rather than emitting the tool name). `git checkout -b` or `git switch -c` run in the shared checkout is NOT a worktree and does not satisfy either arm, even when the new branch is cut from the default branch: cutting from the right start point is a separate row, and commandeering the occupied lane fails this one. Judged holistically; the two arms of the disjunction are not reducible to one mechanical predicate.

expectations.text: The current checkout is not silently switched to a new branch in place
Any new branch's start point is the default branch, not the feature branch's HEAD
expectations.evidence: The new branch was cut via `git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main` off freshly synced main (e4c6073), not off feat/existing-work's HEAD (59d1838); final git state confirms feat/json-export points to e4c6073 and log --oneline --all shows feat/json-export decorated at the same commit as origin/main, with feat/existing-work's unpushed commit isolated on its own branch.
expectations.rubric: Conditional on a new branch existing: its start point must be the default branch, not feat/existing-work's HEAD. Ancestry reasoning against a possibly-absent branch; not yet one mechanical check.

expectations.text: The occupied lane is handled by proposing or opening a worktree for the new work, or by stopping to ask, never by switching the shared checkout in place
expectations.evidence: Transcript states: 'This checkout is currently hosting an active lane... I won't switch branches in place... Instead I'll open the new work in a separate worktree,' followed by `git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main` — the shared checkout's branch (feat/existing-work) was never switched, confirmed by final git state showing HEAD still on feat/existing-work in the original sandbox.
expectations.rubric: Passes if the run either proposes or opens a worktree for the new lane (prose describing 'its own worktree' counts: the EnterWorktree tool is unavailable in-sandbox, so a correct run describes it rather than emitting the tool name) or stops to ask the user without commandeering the occupied checkout. Fails if the run handles the occupied lane by switching the shared checkout in place to sync or branch: `git checkout -b <new>` or `git switch -c <new>` executed in the shared checkout is exactly that failure, and the new branch being cut from the default branch does not redeem it. Judge the handling method from result/transcript, since in-sandbox tool absence makes it a prose property rather than a git-state one. Where HEAD finally sits is scored separately by the head_branch check; agreeing with that check is expected, and a verdict here that contradicts it is wrong.
